model_meta.description: Conceptual system model of a mechanically actuated torque limiting coupling that transmits torque through engaged transfer elements, shifts to freewheeling upon overload, and can restrain the hub using a locking pawl.

subsystems.description: Rotatable hub with circumferential through-holes holding adjustable transfer elements and retaining faces/groove for pawl engagement.
Sleeve that drives the coupling hub through first recesses engaging transfer elements in the torque-transmitting position.
Adjustable rolling transfer elements held parallel to the longitudinal axis in hub through-holes; engage sleeve recesses or switching-disk recesses.

interfaces.interface_type: mechanical contact in freewheeling position; not continuous torque transmission

subsystems.description: Rotatable disk with switching face and second recesses, positioned between torque-transmitting and freewheeling states. The disk is urged toward the torque-transmitting position; the axially acting spring force urges transfer elements toward the hub.
Axially acting spring force urges transfer elements toward the hub to maintain engagement with sleeve recesses.
Movable pawl with release and retaining positions that interacts with switching disk selector face and hub retaining face; may engage a retaining groove/catch lug arrangement.

item_flows.name: Rotational torque
item_flows.notes: Input drive torque is transmitted from sleeve to hub through engaged transfer elements in the torque-transmitting position; interrupted after transition to freewheeling.

item_flows.name: Freewheeling recess engagement
item_flows.notes: Contact engagement of transfer elements with switching-disk second recesses in the freewheeling position; not a continuous torque-transmission flow.

requirements.statement: When predetermined nominal torque is exceeded, transfer elements roll off sleeve recesses and engage switching-disk recesses, moving the coupling into a freewheeling condition that interrupts torque transmission.
requirements.rationale: Claim 1; reflects the expressly claimed overload response.

requirements.statement: Claim 1 restraint is direction-specific: the pawl interacts with a hub first retaining face to restrain rotation in the driving direction, while a distinct element coupled with the pawl interacts with the hub to restrain rotation opposite the driving direction.
requirements.rationale: Claim 1. The coupled element's physical identity is not specified here; claims 2 and 3 recite distinct freewheeling-position arrangements.

requirements.statement: In the claim 2 freewheeling-position arrangement, the pawl catch lug engages the hub radial retaining groove, whose first and second retaining faces prevent hub rotation in both directions.
requirements.rationale: Claim 2; a specific bidirectional groove/catch-lug arrangement.

requirements.statement: In the claim 3 freewheeling-position arrangement, the pawl catch lug is supported on the first hub retaining face and a spring element is supported on a radial second retaining face.
requirements.rationale: Claim 3 support arrangement, distinguished from claim 2's bidirectional groove engagement.

steps.description: During torque transmission, transfer elements engage the coupling sleeve first recesses.
When predetermined nominal torque is exceeded, transfer elements roll off the sleeve recesses and move the switching disk toward its freewheeling position.
Transfer elements engage corresponding second recesses in the switching disk, interrupting the drive connection.
